name: Breakdown: See the Physics
subtitle: Pool that shows its physics
promotional_text: Play eight-ball or nine-ball against the computer, learn the shots in six short lessons, and watch every shot explain itself in slow motion.
keywords: billiards,8 ball,9 ball,lessons,practice,trick shot,bank,jump,masse,bumper,five pin,bar,slow motion
description:
A pool table that shows its physics.

Every shot in Breakdown is worked out by the game's own physics solver, and the table can show you how. Take the cue, play the shot, then switch on the Lens and watch it again in slow motion while the table explains itself.

THE LENS

- Magenta paths where a ball is sliding, cyan where it rolls, thicker when it is fast
- The moment the cloth turns a slide into a roll
- Speed handed from one ball to the next at every hit
- Spin you can see: draw, follow and side
- A plain sentence for each moment that matters, with the equation and the shot's own numbers behind it

Scrub back and forth through any shot, pause it, or ride along with the cue ball. Missed? Try again from the same spot and see exactly what changed.

LEARN IN SIX LESSONS

Stop, follow, draw, cut, curve and jump. Each lesson shows the shot first and why it works, then hands you the cue until you can play it yourself.

PLAY FULL GAMES

Eight-ball and nine-ball with the full rules: calling your shots, fouls, ball in hand, the 8 on the break. Play the computer at easy, medium or hard. The computer shows why it chose each shot, so you learn from it as you play.

THE STROKE

Power is how fast you swing. On a touch screen you pull back from the white ball and push through it, and a rushed or crooked stroke drifts off line. A straight-stroke drill measures yours. You can also play with a mouse, a keyboard or a game controller.

With a stylus, hover over the table to aim, and stand it up as you stroke to raise the cue in free play and games.

TRICK SHOTS AND BEHIND THE 8-BALL

Eleven trick shots: watch each one first, then make it yourself. Behind the 8-Ball drops you into twelve eight-ball spots where you are hooked. Call your ball, then kick, bank, jump or massé your way out, scored for the make, the difficulty and the style, with a card giving the aim, speed and spin the escape used.

THREE OTHER TABLES

Bumper pool, five-pin billiards and bar billiards, each with its own rules and its own score.

TEN SURFACES

Standard and tournament cloth, worn dive-bar felt, then ice, glass, rubber, cork, carpet, sand and the Moon. Your surface carries over to practice and the trick shots, so you can see how the same shot changes.

ALSO IN THE GAME

- A 3D cue that lines up every shot and rises for jumps and massés; the game picks the right cue for a break, a jump or a massé and tells you
- A room around the table, with a lamp over the cloth
- Free practice on any table and surface
- Screen reader support, larger text and controller play
- Twelve languages
- For the curious and the classroom: the physics is shown in metric units, with its equations.

Every path and number on screen is worked out by the game's own solver. None is drawn by hand. There is no chance in it: the same shot always plays out the same way, even a miscue, when the tip slips off the ball.
